items.title: 'The Odyssey' wants you to suffer
items.content:
Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” arrives in theaters this week. And if you thought that “Oppenheimer” was the most Christopher Nolan movie that Christopher Nolan could possibly make, let this serve as either an exciting tease or a stern warning: You ain’t seen squat. Blessed with a reported $250 million budget, the Oscar-winning director has used Homer’s Greek epic to amplify (somehow) all of his trademark directorial tics. Is this movie long? Dude, it is SO long. Does the story center around a taciturn fellow (Matt Damon, never better) who’s got some heavy s—t going on? Absolutely. Do we get a plot timeline that’s been chopped and screwed? Very much so. Is the sound mix deafening, to the point of pain, and are entire swaths of dialogue still not comprehensible despite that loudness? (My answer gets drowned out by Ludwig Göransson’s score).

You get the idea. Cineastes likely formed their opinions about Nolan’s work a long time ago, and nothing about his latest opus will make them, or you, think differently about the man as an artist. Every frame of this movie may as well be sporting a DIRECTED BY CHRISTOPHER NOLAN watermark, such is its maximum Christopher Nolan-ness. But this is what moviegoers pay for. They know that every Nolan movie will be an , that the director will subject them to levels of sensory overload normally reserved for interrogation subjects. They want the pain. 

And so do I. While “Oppenheimer” bored me to death, I’m almost always happy to let Nolan do his thing up on screen, so long as he blows stuff up real good. And folks, “The Odyssey” a lot of stuff blowing up real good, plus kickass battle scenes, man-eating giants and multiple shipwrecks. Like its source material, it’s a story constructed as a series of impossibly huge, explosive set pieces that will make you ooh and ahh, while also sapping every last ounce of energy out of your body. You will be bombarded, exhilarated and entertained in equal measure by these sequences. These scenes have real intellect undergirding them, and they’re as good as blockbuster filmmaking gets.

Article continues below this ad

For the most part. While Nolan doesn’t include every single one of Homer’s trials that Odysseus had to endure to make it home to his wife Penelope (Nolan regular Anne Hathaway) and son Telemachus (Tom Holland), he crams as many of them into the plot as he can. I will now rank these scenes for you, in order from worst to best (warning: spoilers for a thousand-year-old Greek epic ahead).

You might have seen these giant, armor-plated soldiers in the trailer for “The Odyssey” and thought to yourself, “Hey man, that looks insanely cool.” But for those of us who have seen Peter Jackson’s “Lord of the Rings” movies, they’re not a particularly new movie visual. Odysseus’s men land on the island of these cannibals on their way home, see the bigass giants bearing down on them, and then flee back to their ships as fast as they can. There’s a lot of fleeing in this movie.

Article continues below this ad

All of Odysseus’s men are tired and exhausted from sailing the sea and fighting wars, monsters and war monsters. They need to chill out for a second, so they beg Odysseus to let them land on Helios, which is ruled by the sun gods and is populated by endless herds of tasty cattlesheep. And Odie is like, “OK, we can land there, but you can only eat the plants that are around, plus whatever damp hardtack we still have in storage. Don’t eat the beef or else you’ll all die.” Well, they land on Helios and that naughty sun god kills the wind, so that they have to stay marooned there to the brink of starvation. I certainly understood what it felt like to be bored and hungry from this sequence.

Homer’s tale is full of temptresses attempting to lure Odysseus and into their heavenly traps. The most dangerous of the lot is Calypso (Charlize Theron), who captures Odysseus on her isle and lulls him into illusory domestic bliss with her for seven years. She charms Odysseus by feeding him lotus root, which to my eye appears to be about as filling as half a boiled artichoke. But Odysseus seems to like his vegan delight a great deal, and it keeps him swole, so you roll with it. The Calypso scenes serve as a homeroom for our story, as Odysseus recounts to the muse all of the tribulations he had to endure just to make it to her, his final trial before returning home. But, apart from the fantastic location porn, these scenes themselves are fairly rote. The muddled dialogue doesn’t help matters. It’s also annoying that Odysseus can’t tell that he’s being played. I was like WAKE THE F—K UP, YOU DUMMY.

Article continues below this ad

To find his way back home, Odysseus must first travel to the underworld and consult with Tiresias, the blind prophet. This is when our hero must also confront the ghost of his own cousin Sinon (Elliot Page), whom he let die in order to execute the Trojan Horse ruse. Sinon’s ghost, part of an army of the dead that rises out of the volcanic soil, is a little bit cranky with Odysseus about the whole being sacrificed thing. As with other Nolan films, Odysseus is forced to reckon with the damage his choices have made, even when they were the right choices. if they were. This is good, heavy stuff. Then the army of the dead advances and we get more fleeing.

Every Nolan film leaves you crying out for moments of levity. Here was a good one: Odysseus forcing his men to sail through the land of the sirens with their ears plugged with wax, so that they won’t be tempted by the evil sirens’ song. As for Odysseus himself, he refuses the earplugs and has his boys tie him to their ship’s mast. His second-in-charge and best bud Eurylochus (Himesh Patel) warns him that no man has ever heard the song and survived, to which Odie replies, “Then I’ll be the first!” Oh, you complete dumbass. This isn’t a YouTube challenge, this is the wrath of the gods you’re facing down here! Anyway, it was fun to watch the sirens ruin his s—t.

Article continues below this ad

You’re paying to see a Trojan horse scene in this movie, and by God, Nolan gives it to you. Odysseus and his men suffer for days on end hiding inside of the horse until the Trojans, suckers that they are, drag the horse from the beach into their city as a war prize. Then night falls and the Spartans slip out of the horse’s belly (how did the Trojans not notice there was a trap door?) to open the city gates for King Agamemnon (Benny Safdie, wearing one of the more badass costumes I’ve ever seen) and the rest of the Greek army. This siege is shown in bits and pieces throughout the whole film, and it kicks ass every time.

The middle of “The Odyssey” works best when it’s a high-class monster movie, and the twin obstacles of Scylla, the man eating-monster, and Charybdis, the ship-swallowing whirlpool, make for premium monster movie viewing. Because just when Odysseus and his men have dodged Charybdis’ vortex and think they’re in the clear … BOOM! Here comes Scylla out of the mountainside to make an afternoon snack out of them. This is why I would have just flown back home to Ithaca from Troy.

Article continues below this ad

The most gruesome sequence in the movie occurs when Odysseus and his men land on a seemingly pastoral island home to a nice farmer lady named Circe (Samantha Morton, brilliant). Circe offers to feed the starving men, and they happily take her up on the offer. But oopsy daisy, turns out SHE’S A WITCH! Never trust a big cauldron and a smile! Circe feeds the men a cursed poison and turns all of the men into pigs, by hand. It’s extremely surreal and gross. Charlie Kaufman would be proud. Then Odysseus guilt trips the witch into changing his men back. They don’t seem bitter about it.

You’ve seen this one in the trailer, too. It’s the first big action sequence of “The Odyssey,” and it’s a doozy as Odysseus and his men land on yet another cursed isle (are there NO normal isles in this sea? Jesus!) and follow a lone sheep there into a cave. Now, you and I know better than to go heading into spooky caves, but not these guys. They head right on in and get rewarded with having to fight a one-eyed giant (Bill Irwin) with a crooked nose and no pants. The cyclops grabs a lot of the men and eats them. Did I whoop when Odysseus and his men jabbed a flaming log directly into Cyclops’ eye socket? Sure did. This part ruled.

Article continues below this ad

It takes a very, very long time for Damon’s Odysseus to finally make it home to Ithaca. It takes him so long, in fact, that I wondered if Nolan was telling this story in real time. But despite all the fat that Nolan leaves on screen throughout “The Odyssey” — they easily could have cut 20 minutes from the movie and not lost anything — the wait ends up paying off. Odysseus has arrived home only to discover that his palace has been overrun by nasty suitors led by the cowardly Antinous (Robert Pattinson, in a role he was born to play), who has spent Odysseus’s sabbatical trying to coerce Hathaway’s Penelope into marrying him. That weasely little s—t.

Article continues below this ad

With no army at his disposal, Odysseus has to disguise himself as a beggar to enter the palace and ingratiate himself, best he can, with Antinous and his looksmaxxing crew. Nolan makes you wait, and wait, and wait for Odysseus to finally reveal himself to everyone. It’s suspenseful to the point of torture. But when Ionnis Wick finally takes off his hood and is like, “Yeah, I think I’m back,” the theater I watched this flick in detonated. Cheering. Clapping. Hooting. All of it. We had survived Nolan’s film together, and this was our reward for it. It was worth it. You’ll never see a movie quite like this until Nolan makes his next one. Four stars.

Editor's note: This story was updated on July 15 at 10:10 a.m. to correct an error about the Trojan War.

items.title: If you don't hate data centers yet, boy do I have news for you
items.content:
I was watching some hot World Cup action the other day when this local ad from a lobbying group called Virginia Connects graced my television screen. I didn’t know that Virginia Connects was behind this spot until the very end of it, which is standard practice for all evilmongers these days. If I see a commercial that begins with a tasteful montage of Americans doing super-serious, deeply American things, that ad will inevitably end with a plug for AI, Meta pinky-swearing to keep your kids safe, or a promise that Jesus gets me.

This Virginia Connects ad plays out in a similar fashion. It opens with an all-American dad using his smartphone to give his all-American wife (who’s also a troop, naturally) the play-by-play of their son’s baseball game. It’s all generically wholesome enough until the final three seconds, when a warm voice-over tells the audience:

Article continues below this ad

“Virginia’s data centers. Connecting us with what matters most.”

Go ahead and let out a long, pained groan. I know I did.

This ad represents a somewhat belated push by the tech industry to fight back against Americans’ growing distaste for data centers. That Virginia Connects ad I linked to? It’s no coincidence that the people behind it disabled YouTube comments under it. Even hate data centers now. Save for Donald Trump, naturally. No, the president can’t get enough of these wonderful structures. He’s actively castigating the numerous lawmakers and citizens alike who oppose data centers and are, in increasing numbers, imposing bans on their construction. Your home state of California hates data centers. Georgia hates them. Virginia hates them, despite the troop baseball mom on TV feeling otherwise. And New York state just imposed a moratorium on their construction, which really got Trump upset, as evidenced by this online rant he fired off direct from his gold-plated Mar-a-Lago toilet:

“Data Centers are tremendous WINS for the States and Communities that are lucky enough to get them. New York should change its Policy, IMMEDIATELY. The Radical Left Dumocrats must not be allowed to cause us to lose Data Centers, AI, and all of this incredible new Technology, to China, and other countries! President DONALD J. TRUMP.”

Article continues below this ad

Alas, this incredibly cogent and well-reasoned plea on behalf of data centers from Trump has failed to sway public sentiment in favor of building more of them. Americans, myself included, despise these things. And so should you. Let me tell you why.

Superficially speaking, a data center isn’t much to be worked up over. It’s essentially a warehouse for data storage. A server farm, same as the ones that have undergirded your internet and mine for the bulk of this century. AWS, Cloudflare, Google Cloud: These companies and others house the vast majority of online data that Americans use as part of their daily lives. Until a couple of years ago, this country’s existing server farms were sufficient enough to handle all of that data. So why, all of a sudden, are tech companies falling all over themselves to build so many more of them, and as quickly as they can? Time for another long, pained groan out of you. From the International Business Times:

“Major technology firms are increasingly leaning on complex financial engineering to fund their $3 trillion AI infrastructure build-out.” And later on in the piece: “Analysts point to similar arrangements involving not only data center construction but chip and energy purchases, where combined commitments across top tech firms now top $1.8 trillion, outstripping their $1.4 trillion in recorded balance sheet liabilities.”

Article continues below this ad

That’s right. All of these data centers aren’t being built to connect you, the normal person, to what matters most. They’re intended to connect you to big tech’s AI ecosystem, which itself was designed to from what matters most, namely other people and the collective intellectual, emotional and spiritual value that humans have provided one another throughout humankind’s existence. AI is, at its core, an evil product that’s been engineered to wean human beings off needing, not to mention loving, one another. Its implantation is the ultimate consolidation effort by a tech class that means to horde everything — every dollar you’ve saved, every minute of your time, every idea inside your head — for itself.

Therefore, data centers — bland, inert structures that add no aesthetic or intellectual value to the landscape they’re built on — stand as the physical embodiment of the AI sector’s grotesque avariciousness. They also require so much power to run that they’ve already created a supply crisis, which has resulted in higher power bills for millions of Americans, myself included (our power bill last month was $400). According to one credible report, these structures could use a fifth of the nation’s power less than a decade from now. They could quadruple their water usage within just two years. All for a bunch of faceless buildings that don’t even crank out toys, or motorcycles, or some other sort of cool product.

And the funny part (kinda) is that data centers barely even make their owners a profit! This building frenzy is kicking into overdrive just as the AI bubble is visibly bursting at the seams. OpenAI is on pace to miss its revenue projections by 90% over the next five years. The indispensable tech blogger Ed Zitron reports that, in nearly the same span of time, OpenAI will burn through nearly a trillion dollars in funding, with no hope of even coming close to earning enough revenue to make up the difference. That means that OpenAI and its cohorts (Microsoft, Oracle, Amazon and more) are blighting the landscape and drinking your milkshake in service of a revolution that’s already dead on arrival. And guess who they’ll ask for a bailout when it all goes to s—t? It won’t be each other. It’ll be you and me.

Article continues below this ad

This is waste on an unimaginable scale. And if our tech overlords aren’t kept in check, they’ll waste everything we have. Don’t let them.

items.title: The new Anya Taylor-Joy vehicle is so stupid and so good
items.content:
Veteran couch potatoes know that Apple TV is currently the best streaming service. Netflix is a year away from casting Tilly Norwood in every series. HBO Max is still being run by a slash-and-burn expert whose sense of the zeitgeist is stuck somewhere around 1990. And Paramount+ is populated almost exclusively by 44-minute pickup ads. I can’t count on any of the aforementioned streamers to actually care about my needs as an educated viewer. Apple TV, for whatever reason, does. 

That brings us to “Lucky,” based on Marissa Stapley’s pulp novel and starring Anya Taylor-Joy as the title character. “Lucky” is four episodes into its inaugural season. It isn’t highbrow content. In fact, it’s probably one of the more idiotic shows I’ve elected to binge-watch lately. It also might be the best TV show I’ll watch all year, because few other shows are as willing to lean into their inherent absurdity as much as this one.

Article continues below this ad

Here’s some spoiler-y proof. Our story opens in Vegas, where Taylor-Joy’s Lucky and her boy toy Cary (Drew Starkey, whose face you’ll hate) have just stolen a whole bunch of cash from an unknown source and are unwisely celebrating their windfall instead of running very far away, very quickly. Lucky wakes up the next morning to discover that the hubby has ghosted her and taken the millions with him. When Lucky needs to flee the scene before the cops, or a shady mob guy with shady mob guy product in his hair, find her, she cannily disguises herself in designer jeans and a designer hoodie, and hey presto! She DISAPPEARS out of the casino. Then she stops off to give herself a flawless DIY cut-and-color so she can look like a  traffic-stopping style icon than she looked like before. Even when Anya Taylor-Joy gets her ass kicked and is locked inside a car trunk, she still absolutely looks like Anya Taylor-Joy. You and I could spot that face from a mile away. Then Lucky crashes a rich lady’s cocktail party, steals all of the swag lying around the house, and walks out of there looking like she’s about to walk a Paris runway. Now you and I could spot her from a solar system away.

But the cops and mobsters can’t! “Lucky” includes a lot of Stupid Guy Show stock characters. In addition to the oily mob enforcer (Clifton Collins Jr.), we’ve got an FBI agent who takes this case way too personally (Aunjanue Ellis-Taylor), her whipping boy sidekick who has shrewder hunches than the boss expected (Mo McRae), and a ruthless mobster played by an acclaimed actor overqualified for the role (Annette Bening). Bening, who’s great in everything, is Cary’s mother. And Cary, we later find out, is actually married to Lucky. That makes Bening Lucky’s mother-in-law. She also just happens to be fresh out of jail and wrapped up in an ambiguous fossil fuel scam (I think?). Oh, and it’s money that Lucky and her man stole. Hence, Bening’s Priscilla Masterson wants Lucky dead, and she also might want her traitor son dead too. Because Priscilla isn’t the top gasoline mafioso in LA. She reports to a guy named Wayne (William Fichtner), and it’s HIS money that she was tasked with overseeing. Now Wayne is pissed, and you don’t want a William Fichtner character pissed.

Meanwhile, Lucky’s dad (Timothy Olyphant) is a small-time crook stuck in jail whom Lucky periodically rings up for advice on doing crimes. It takes a few episodes for the old man to tell Lucky, “Hey man, maybe it’s unwise to hash out your fugitive getaway plans when this jail phone is probably tapped,” but by then, I didn’t care. I was too busy enjoying all of these great actors chewing on every available piece of scenery in between big action set pieces. And when the show got REALLY stupid this past week and veered into pure soap opera territory, I became even more invested. Was I surprised when I found out that all of these characters share a history with one another? No. Did I laugh out loud when Lucky’s husband hides the stolen cash by converting all of it to bitcoin? Did I ever! Drew Starkey has a face for crypto, and showrunner Jonathan Tropper was wise to exploit it.

Article continues below this ad

Tropper is no stranger to dad movie-level entertainment. He was the guy behind “Banshee,” a great not-so-smart action show created by Warner Bros. in the 2010s in an ill-fated attempt to create a Cinemax original programming brand apart from HBO. Apple TV gives Tropper a more prestigious imprimatur this time around, much in the same way it does with another Tropper creation, the Jon Hamm vehicle “Your Friends and Neighbors.” But with both that show and “Lucky,” Tropper doesn’t let his new home give him any airs of pretension. “Lucky” starts off trashy and never lets up. When I spotted a spare screwdriver lying around in one critical scene, I immediately thought, “Someone is gonna get stabbed in the head with that thing.” Minutes later, my prescience was rewarded. That screwdriver was Chekhov’s screwdriver.

There is an art to this kind of show. It’s not something you can create by asking an AI prompt to make it for you. And it’s not something that you can entrust to just any random showrunner, or just any random, Gal Gadot-level actor in your cast. No no, a show like “Lucky” takes real work. It takes a quietly excellent writing staff (Priscilla on her son: “I still have to kill spiders for him”), an executive producer with serious creative juice (Reese Witherspoon, who chose the “Lucky” novel for her book club in 2021), and a magnetic cast. “Lucky” has all of those things going for it. In fact, it’s not unlike Apple’s most recent Emmy nominee, “Widow’s Bay,” which is also quite silly (Yar! This island be cursed!) but also boasts a murderers’ row of actors (with global treasure Matthew Rhys at its center) and a creative team that takes the show’s premise as seriously as if it were staging a production of “Hamlet.”

Article continues below this ad

Both of those shows, along with HBO Max’s “The Pitt,” are establishing a new genre of middlebrow entertainment, one that echoes the great middlebrow network programs of yore while also elevating the genre by using prestige TV-level talent. No one is gonna mistake “Lucky” for “Mad Men” anytime soon, but not every TV show has to be some landmark entry into the canon. Sometimes a TV show can just be a TV show, and “Lucky” excels at being just that.

items.title: Craiglist's founder on why he left San Francisco and the plans for his billions
items.content:
If you’re wondering whether there are any good people remaining in the tech sector, or in this country’s ruling class in general, you’d be hard pressed to find a better case study than Craig Newmark. Newmark founded Craigslist.org in San Francisco way back in 1996 and became the sort of accidental billionaire that the early dot-com boom cranked out with seeming regularity. Some of those billionaires went on to become evil (Mark Zuckerberg), and some of them ended up merely becoming rich loud guys (Mark Cuban). Newmark, who ceded his CEO duties at Craigslist shortly after its founding, has endeavored to keep a lower profile, and a lower net worth, than any of them.

To wit: Newmark no longer works with Craigslist at all, and spends the bulk of his time tending to various philanthropic endeavors. He doesn’t own a pro sports team, doesn’t own a loud superyacht, and doesn’t stage vanity runs for president. He’s given away much of his wealth and signed Bill Gates’ Giving Pledge to give away at least half his career earnings before he dies. He also dresses like a common schlub, so much so that you probably wouldn’t recognize the man if you passed by him on the street. This willful anonymity makes Newmark a seeming outlier among his peers, which he almost certainly prefers. In fact, he refers to himself in conversation as a “peasant” on repeated occasions, just to drive home the idea that despite his largesse — both in money given away and money saved — he’s just like you and me. He’s earned billions in his lifetime, but insists he’s no longer worth that much, which means I shouldn’t technically call him a “billionaire.”  

But isn’t he? After all, once you’ve made a billion, you can’t unmake it. And even if you give all of your money away, aren’t you still a billionaire in spirit? I met with Newmark at his office space in New York this week to find out.

Article continues below this ad

Newmark works in a nondescript office inside of the Civic Hall community center, just off of Union Square. There are plenty of other people working in the open area of this floor, but they don’t work for Newmark, nor do they bother to greet him as we pass them by. He escorts me to his private office space, located in a hallway just off the bullpen. It’s a Spartan room, decorated only with canvas printouts of photos that Newmark or his wife Eileen have taken. Many of the photos are of wild pigeons that the Newmarks have fed over the years, including a recently deceased one that Craig named Ghostface Killah. There’s also a framed triptych featuring a photo of infamous libertarian novelist Ayn Rand flanked by copies of the first and last handwritten pages of her manuscript for “Atlas Shrugged.” This could be anyone’s office, and Newmark, sitting before me, could be any random white-collar worker. Our ensuing conversation has been edited for length and clarity.

When did Ghostface Killah pass away?

Guessing around a year ago. He would see one of us out the window and come waddling over. A pigeon walk is never graceful.

Article continues below this ad

We still have a place in San Francisco and we put bird food out, which is also unintentionally sometimes raccoon food or coyote food. We live on one edge of Sutro Forest, right next to the hospital. Near the hospital. Apparently, the raccoon is named Larry.

No, the raccoon named himself. The coyote, most frequently showing up, is also Larry.

You moved to New York full time five years ago. Why did you leave San Francisco?

Article continues below this ad

There’s more going on for me in philanthropy in this part of the country. A lot more. Also, we have family issues like aging in-laws who are in New Jersey right now. Let’s say there’s a comfortable place awaiting them and my sister-in-laws in Long Island. Is that a tactful phrasing?

Yes. I’ve been there. How did you like living in San Francisco when you did live there?

I really like it, both now and then.

Do you like present-day San Francisco? Do you feel like the city’s changed in any significant way since you founded Craigslist?

Article continues below this ad

It has changed a lot. The industry is very young now. I don’t relate well to that. Also, my favorite coffee place on Cole Street is gone.

Reverie. Like a dream. I’m hoping the new place which just opened up, Double Black, works. I need a new hangout. In fact, please put that in the article.

Why is there more philanthropy going on in NYC for you than in San Francisco? What’s the difference?

Article continues below this ad

Very little in my interest areas happens in San Francisco, but a lot happens either in New York or Washington, or the people from the nonprofits or funders either live and work here or visit New York a lot.

What are those interests?

Well I’m still an amateur when it comes to philanthropy.

I’m not sure I believe you.

Article continues below this ad

Let’s say I’m shrinking my ignorance less and less all the time, sometimes embarrassing myself.

You’d be the rare billionaire willing to embarrass yourself.

Well, I have given up on pride and dignity. For sure, I don’t care. I’ve admitted to myself over the last year or two that I do have the tastes and attitudes of a peasant. I am a peasant with money, but I’m still a peasant. I’m still learning a lot. I figured I would do work where I’m doing some good, which the two big areas are now military families and veterans. I’m now working with people to plan out my giving through 2033. I’ve outsourced almost all my best work and my family’s work to Bob Woodruff Foundation and Blue Star Families. That’s Bob Woodruff, the ABC guy. He was blown up by an IED. The deal is I’ve committed $200 million to families and vets, and I’m halfway there.

Is that direct help? Because you said Washington’s part of it, so how much of it is lobbying efforts too?

Article continues below this ad

None of what I’m doing is lobbying. It’s vetting and funding vets groups who are actually good at something.

What do you mean by “actually good at something”?

They actually provide actual help for vets. In our country, there are many nonprofits still on the books who are either defunct or don’t get much done. The Bob Woodruff people are good.

Shouldn’t there be some lobbying component to it though, because philanthropy can only get you so far? Don’t you have to be on the side of enacting that help these people too?

Article continues below this ad

I don’t know. Even if the government steps up more, philanthropists have got to step up because there are vets and spouses who need help. I mean, right now. Today.

Right. But in an ideal world, we wouldn’t have to rely on the kindness of people such as yourself. We would have a Department of Defense and a federal government that takes care of its own.

I like the idea, but I have to defer to people who know the stuff. My experience has been, when it comes to anything Washington-related, I’m just way out of my depth immediately.

Are you out of your depth? You’re not dumb.

Article continues below this ad

I am when it comes to things like communications. I’ve learned the hard way that a person who’s honest is never going to be a match for someone who lies for a living. The deal is that the small guys need help. You might be thinking government needs to do that. New York State just made an announcement, by coincidence, a few days ago, because you may have read how Iran has compromised or attacked a bunch of water supplies, particularly in Minnesota and elsewhere. The feds are mostly sure it’s Iran, not 100%.

Do you believe the feds when they say that?

Article continues below this ad

Because I know and trust some of them, and even better, the people I support who are the real experts are working with government.

Do those people predate this current administration?

Yes. Some of those folks have been doing it for decades. The idea is that there will be an announcement, a real serious one, Friday. (Editor’s note: This refers to Friday, Aug. 7, during which there was no substantial Iran announcement.)

You’ve long said you’re bad at picking up on social cues. That you’re not really a great communicator, so you outsource it to other people. However, isn’t that also basically a form of self-protection? Isn’t the best way to counteract all of those lies not silence, but to speak the truth?

Article continues below this ad

You’d hope so. Sometimes it does, and more frequently it doesn’t. That’s a really big topic when it comes to my support for journalism. I’ve already put a couple hundred million into that. The money best spent has been on the CUNY journalism school and Wikipedia. I have a researcher acquaintance at Penn who wrote a book saying that Craigslist and Wikipedia are the last ungentrified sites on the internet. Everything else has gotten fancy, expensive, and as author Cory Doctorow would say, ens—ttified. I’ve known Cory for a long time. Cory has done really important, big-deal work, but I’m just not up to it. He’s just much better than I am.

Is it that you’re not up to it, or you would just prefer to just chill?

I’ve given up being good at it. I’m 73, and I’m very aware of my limitations. The deal is that the CUNY J-school is a big deal for me because CUNY has been providing opportunities for New Yorkers who would never get a break otherwise. I have to think about renewing a commitment I have for the CUNY Wikipedia person-in-residence because there’s a Wikipedia chapter in New York, and they run programs like teaching people how to edit Wikipedia, which is a really big deal because Wikipedia makes user-generated content work way better than anyone does.

Article continues below this ad

But it needs more editors. And brave ones, because sometimes they get attacked.

Do you ever edit Wikipedia stuff?

You don’t look at your own entry and feel tempted to edit?

Article continues below this ad

I have to be really good about practicing the community ethics, which means I don’t touch my page or the Craigslist page. When I want something corrected or updated, I beg for help. I do need updating on the matter of cops and constitutional rights, because I am going public with my support for fighting human trafficking. The NYPD people have said to me, “Well, the bomb squad needs funding for protective gear and radios which aren’t vulnerable to jamming.” I said, “Well, if there’s guys going to be going out there to protect me from bombs, I guess I could spare something.” I’ve done that.

Do you believe them when they tell you that, because police department budgets are quite robust, particularly here in New York?

Not as robust as you think, and it’s tough. Frankly, I think cops should be paid more.

Article continues below this ad

They don’t make enough to afford to live here in many cases (Editor's note: according to GovSalaries, the median salary for an NYPD officer is just over $91,000). In a lot of New York, rent is like $5,000 to $10,000 a month.

Yeah, but no one can afford to live here.

Well, that’s a long separate discussion.

Article continues below this ad

For students at the J-school, I can help make the school tuition free. That’s a good use of money. The school needs to raise some more money, and I want to help them do that, but that involves talking to donors, and that involves social skills. Again, I’m not good at that.

You’re talking to me eloquently now, though. You can be persuasive, surely.

I’ve been practicing, and I’m not good in particular at talking with people who have money. I’m a peasant attitudinally, even though I have money, much less than people think, because a few years ago I put all my Craigslist shares into a 501(c)(4).

Article continues below this ad

This is part of your giving pledge?

Yes. I’ve now given away $550 million. With my commitments, I’m at $660 million.

My fantasy is by the time I pass and I’m replaced by AI Craig, I will have given away $1 billion, in large part due to the miracle of compound interest.

Article continues below this ad

I wanted to ask you about the Giving Pledge, because isn’t it a way to discourage lawmakers from taxing billionaires at the proper rate that they should be taxed? You understand how, particularly someone like me who’s a journalist who has had to deal with the hope of benevolent billionaires saving my industry and having that fail quite spectacularly, you understand why I might be disillusioned, even talking to you, someone who is very earnest about fulfilling the Giving Pledge, about your class of people? I know you think you’re a peasant, but you’ve earned what you’ve earned.

I’m both a peasant and a fairly well-off guy.

I’m Schrödinger’s philanthropist. I’m in both states at once. I’ve thought about these issues, and I realize they’re a waste of my time to think about because I can’t do anything. Meanwhile, I can do something about other matters.

Article continues below this ad

Why do you think you can’t do anything?

All I can do usefully is to give away money, make some noise about it, and then focus on an area where I can do something, like fighting scams.

Isn’t that a tacit acceptance that you as an individual can’t do anything to help make the world a bit more fair than it currently is?

I’m doing that already in the areas where I focus, like for military families and vets. That’s something where I’m having a real effect. And  I can refrain from opening my big mouth where I don’t know what I’m talking about. When it’s bulls—t, we would be better off if they didn’t say anything.

Article continues below this ad

Yes, but unfortunately, our current ruling class is pretty much entirely comprised of bulls—tters.

I am aware that the signal-to-noise ratio could be vastly improved. All I can do is do something good and talk about it. I am trying to not be cranky and judgmental, unless it’s funny.

Yes. Well, there are times when I judge inappropriately, and I know that sometimes I’m very wrong and unfair to people, so the species is better off if I keep my mouth shut.

Article continues below this ad

I know you’re very, very serious about protecting journalism. Have you reckoned with Craigslist’s role in harming journalism as an industry, particularly in the classified ads section?

I used to be convinced that Craigslist had a significant effect. But in 2018, an industry analyst named Thomas Baekdal ran the numbers. He tells me that the newspaper’s problem started in the ’60s with TV news. He published a chart showing that it was just downhill from there. 

Who’s Baekdal affiliated with?

No one. He’s an independent Swedish guy. He ran the numbers, checked the facts, and told me that the dot-com stuff, including Craigslist, had no effect until 2008 or so when Facebook and Google started cutting into the business.

Article continues below this ad

That’s one study, though. Did you find other studies that corroborated what Baekdal found?

None. There was a guy at NYU who did some good work, but it’s been misinterpreted by everyone. I’m flattering myself if I say that Craigslist didn’t have a measurable effect. Now, I’m not 100% convinced it didn’t, but I need to follow the evidence.

The evidence works in your favor, though. Isn’t it a temptation to believe it to exonerate yourself?

I don’t view it as exoneration or anything. I’ve now spent a decade talking to professional fact-checkers and people like that, and they tell me, “Look at the facts.”

Article continues below this ad

Tell me your thoughts on crypto and AI.

Crypto, I just don’t know. I do like the idea of it.

Article continues below this ad

Well, it’s the part of me that studied libertarianism 50 years ago, early ’70s. Sometimes citizens in dictatorships need alternative currencies, that kind of thing. It has its good purposes, and there have been a lot of scams.

It’s untraceable money. You use it for arms dealing, drug dealing, bribery.

That’s interesting, and I will then focus my limited attention on areas where I can do something about.

As someone who started looking at AI in some form 60 years ago, I’m both fascinated by what’s happening and a little embarrassed that I took my attention elsewhere. When ChatGPT came around, I was completely caught by surprise.

Article continues below this ad

I do tinker with it. Mrs. Newmark is better at it than I am because she’s using it for both real estate and medical issues.

Is it wise to be consulting ChatGPT about medical issues?

Well, it is wise to use AI search. You choose your vendor. Take a look at what AI search says, and then run it by your doctor. What she and I both do is say, “Hey, we’ve taken a look. Why don’t you tell us what’s real?” That works.

Article continues below this ad

What value is there in consulting AI before verifying it with a doctor when you can just go to the doctor?

Since I have a little hypochondria, what I’ll do is I’ll look up something, and it will tell me don’t panic. I’ve got a doctor’s appointment scheduled in six weeks. I’m speaking literally right now. I can wait the six weeks. So I’m very excited about what AI can do, but there are some serious shortcomings. The problem is bad actors doing search engine optimization, and also foreign state actors planting a lot of bad information on the web. If an AI search engine has trained on that misinformation, it’s going to repeat misinformation. The AI search people are acting in good faith to deal with that.

I’ve spoken with them back-channel, and I’ll respect the back channel.

Article continues below this ad

Does that include Sam Altman, Elon Musk?

I don’t know the big guys personally. I talk to the worker people, and they’re working in good faith.

But they’re taking orders from people like Elon and Sam, who may not be perceived as having good faith with these products.

Article continues below this ad

The deal is that I work with people who do what they can, and I’m not going to compromise them.

Isn’t that self-limiting, though?

Yes. It is frustrating because my bias is towards transparency, but I don’t want to get anyone hurt.

Do you believe that there can be a good outcome with AI as opposed to what’s happening right now, in terms of energy usage, students who use AI to cheat, children who have been encouraged to die by suicide by these chatbots, things like that?

Article continues below this ad

As you’ve seen, my strategy is find people who know what they’re doing and are doing a good job. That’s Common Sense Media, which is based in the Bay Area. They do good, so I help fund them. Again, the idea is knowing my limitations and helping out.

You keep saying you know your limitations, but you’re Craig Newmark. You created Craigslist. I can’t help but think that you are using your own modesty as a way of distancing yourself.

I am using what you’re calling my modesty for two reasons. Because it’s funny, and honest, and because I am a nerd, 1950s style.

Article continues below this ad

You do understand that people who are dirt poor, they hear a billionaire say, “Oh, well, I’m just a nerd,” and they roll their eyes. You know?

I am not, nor have I ever been, a billionaire.

OK. All right. A very wealthy man.

I have the luxuries that I want. As an old guy, that includes a walk-in shower with a grab bar. I can subscribe to all the streaming services I want because I love TV. When I want to buy a book, I don’t hesitate. That’s about it.

Article continues below this ad

Otherwise, I think you would consider yourself to be an accidental mogul.

But I think that whether you like it or not, having the amount of money you’ve earned, billions or not, with that comes inherently a great amount of responsibility that perhaps you would prefer not to shoulder entirely.

In terms of shouldering things, if someone else can do the job better than I can, I will share funding and influence with them.

Article continues below this ad

Are you afraid that if you set your social ambitions higher in terms of change, are you afraid of failure?

I am afraid of failure in that sense, but I already could console myself with the notion that Craigslist is a success for regular people. It helps you get through the day with what’s important, like a job or a place to live or a table. In the longer run, Craigslist is good because it showed tens of millions of Americans the internet is good for something and reasonably easy to use. In terms of my stuff now, it looks like I’m doing some real good. Wikipedia is a big deal for the species. It’s like Encyclopedia Galactica, even though they don’t have a good way of showing that on the Apple show, which I recommend. For that matter, I think “Ted Lasso” is back today. (Editor’s note: By “the Apple show,” Newmark is referring to “Foundation,” which features an encyclopedia containing all knowledge.)

I like Apple TV. They’re pretty reliable. I think they’re the best streaming service.

I agree. In terms of especially original content. Like “Silo” is great, “Severance,” oh, and “Slow Horses.”

Article continues below this ad

I’ve now spoken to people at high levels in the U.K. government privately, and they assure me that “Slow Horses” is entirely accurate in terms of the vibe. My colleagues who know better over there did introduce me to I think the minister of defence for a while during Iraq. I can say that the U.S.’s involvement was unfortunate, and that may have been due to maneuvering due to a foreign adversary.

Can you be more specific?

Article continues below this ad

It was demonstrably a s—t war.

Again, my theme is that I can do something constructive, and that is supporting veterans. That’s why I talk to journalists, because by saying things, maybe I could influence people with a lot of extra money to pony up some dough.

But you only say so much.

When I was at IBM, I learned that as a leader by the top management, I completely suck.

Article continues below this ad

I’m just not good at it.

Leadership requires the ability to inspire people. I don’t have that. That’s why I stepped down as CEO at Craigslist.

Article continues below this ad

What were your shortcomings?

I had no people skills.

No, but I could be an asshole.

Article continues below this ad

I would correct people with other people around. Rudely.

Would you just be curt, or screaming?

Article continues below this ad

Curt. I never was the screaming type. That’s not my temperament, ever.

You still buy things off of Craigslist?

Once in a while, Mrs. Newmark will do that kind of thing. That’s all delegated to her. Of course, we’re heavy users of e-commerce as well.

You have favorite websites?

Article continues below this ad

For commerce, it depends on what I’m trying to do. In roughly a week, I have a feeling I’ll be buying a new Google phone since my phone is my main computer.

You’re a Google phone user and not an Apple phone user? Why?

Android is more flexible for my purposes, and I’m a bit of a contrarian.

Article continues below this ad

items.title: California is on fire and these people are profiting off it
items.content:
Wildfires are once again eating their way across California. Three fires, one near Big Sur, one enveloping Lassen and Sierra counties and one raging in Humboldt County, have burned tens of thousands of acres of land, poisoned endangered condors, and closed off various highways and state parks indefinitely. The aforementioned fires have barely been contained by authorities. When (or, *shudder*, if) the fires die down, more fires will follow in their wake. And more after that, and more after that. Wildfire is a natural part of California’s environment, and thanks to humankind’s disastrous warping of the planet’s climate, fires will only grow more widespread and destructive in the years to come.

Now, woke types might tell you that all of this is bad. But what if I told you that the ongoing self-immolation of Earth could help you win BIG MONEY? Because thanks to the advent of prediction markets, you can literally bet on the next fire that’ll strike, like a few lucky sharps did with the LA wildfires of 2025! From Wednesday’s Washington Post:

Article continues below this ad

According to that same WaPo report, some of the Polymarket bettors coyly told each other that they hoped their bets would go bust. You know, like when your fantasy football team goes up against Brock Purdy and you, the woebegone Niners fan, have to hope and also kinda not hope that Purdy sucks that day. It’s basically the same dilemma. Sure, it’s sad to watch thousands of people be displaced from their homes while entire ecosystems get wiped out by an unstoppable conflagration. On the other hand, boy you sure could use some extra scratch to help pay down your F-150! And while Polymarket says that American users can’t trade on wildfires, its users very much can. So all you need is a VPN, or a shady friend in Hungary, to place your bet from “overseas” and you’re in on the action! Then you can go flick a lit Marlboro into a patch of dry grass at Yosemite and :flames emoji:!

“A White House teleprompter operator who was put on unpaid leave after news reports he had used inside knowledge to make bets about President Donald Trump’s speeches on the online prediction market Kalshi is no longer in his post, according to a White House official.”

Article continues below this ad

Sure, the teleprompter guy lost his job because of those bets, but I bet (pun intended!) he won himself one hell of a golden parachute to fall back on!

You and I already know that, under President Barfbag, corruption in America has proliferated at an astonishing rate. But hey man, why let the big pigs feed at the trough when you can get your own taste of that sweet, delicious slop? Thanks to Kalshi, Polymarket, and potential coming rivals like Meta, you and I can finally rig the game in favor! And all it will cost us is the fate of the world! Now that’s an offer that you and I can’t refuse. Because when the powers that be decide to openly ransack the country, it only makes sense for the powerless to see if they can get a small cut of their own. After all, you have nothing to lose if you have no future. So if you’re done with clean air, social services and functional democracy, then put down some cash and watch the world burn. What else do you have to lose?

items.title: Anthony Bourdain loved this San Francisco burger and so do I
items.content:
This is not the correct time for me to be visiting Sam’s Burgers. It’s the middle of the afternoon here in North Beach, and finding a spot inside Sam’s tight confines isn’t much of a problem. If I were to walk in here 12 hours from now, just before the bars close and after patrons of all the nearby strip clubs have no more rain to make … well then, I probably wouldn’t be able to walk in here at all. There would probably be a line going outside the door. There would probably be an ass parked in every bright red leather stool at the counter and in the scant number of booths lining the wall. There would probably be dozens of hungry partiers, some of them quite famous, crowding into the place to eat a cheeseburger at the proper time to be eating a cheeseburger.

That’s when Anthony Bourdain would have come here. In fact, that’s the time of night when he come here, 14 years ago.

“Tony,” a film that serves as a kind of Bourdain origin story, opened in theaters this month, with “Holdovers” standout Dominic Sassa playing the title role. And if you think the studio was a little bit presumptuous in simply naming the film “Tony” — as if Bourdain were the Tony of all Tonys — this midday nosh I’m having at Sam’s is a good indicator that its decision was more prescient than foolhardy. Because even after his death in 2018, Bourdain’s kingmaking powers in the hospitality industry are still robust. I wouldn’t be here otherwise. The man’s name adorns the main page of the Sam’s website, the front window of the restaurant, and the menu, where you can order the Anthony Bourdain Special: a $23.99 cheeseburger/fries/beer combo meal. Bourdain’s image graces the restaurant’s merch, hanging on the wall behind the counter. And if you’re still hungry and still loaded, you can go next door to the new Legends Café & Creamery to order a Bourdain shake and stare at a mural of Tony that occupies the entire wall behind the counter . The Shawa family, which owns both Sam’s and Legends, is milking the Bourdain name for all its worth.

Article continues below this ad

They’re right to, because that name remains valuable in ways that will likely never be replicated. Consider that Bourdain made Sam’s famous by appearing here, very drunk on camera, for a total of roughly five minutes at the tail end of an episode of his short-lived Travel Channel series “The Layover.” Bourdain stumbled into the place, ordered a double cheeseburger, declared, “That is a good motherf—king burger,” and that was all the restaurant needed to prosper afterward. Bourdain lived the kind of life that made the audience want to follow in his many, many footsteps. To travel all the places he traveled, to sample all of the street meat he sampled, and to savor the kind of greasy dining establishments that he savored so fully. That’s why I’m here. It ain’t after hours, but a cheeseburger suits me at any time of day, so time to get my Bourdain on.

Article continues below this ad

The menu at Sam’s remains spare: burgers, fries, rings, Polish sausage, wings, nuggets, hot dogs, fish and chips, fried shrimp and corn dogs. That’s it. If you want a salad, you have the rest of California at your disposal. If you need to take a leak, well then you better head out to an alley because there’s no bathroom here. If you want a beer, OK yes they have beer, you lush. Otherwise, you come here for a burger, and for nothing else.

So I order a double cheeseburger. And a Polish. And some fries and rings, because they have them. I take a seat in one of the booths and rest my back against the warped wood paneling. Behind the grill is a framed photo of restaurant founder Mike Shawa, who died 10 years ago and left control of the restaurant to his surviving family members, with son Emad ElShawa controlling the day-to-day operations. The back walls are covered in old front pages of the San Francisco Chronicle sports section, including one from the 49ers’ 55-10 Super Bowl win over Denver back in 1990. The linoleum flooring is worn and dirty from decades of foot traffic. And the sign hanging outside the restaurant still boasts “burgers and pizza,” even though Sam’s no longer serves pizza. I would’ve ordered the pizza too, but 3,000 calories worth of other food will have to suffice.

It does. The Polish arrives first, split open on a thick roll and topped with the usual peppers and onions. The sausage tastes like sausage. The bun is good, but there’s too much of it. I save my appetite for the coming burger, which is a smart move because the Sam’s double is thicker than a dictionary, with two all-beef patties topping the lettuce and tomato underneath. I take a bite, and yep, that’s a good motherf—king burger. It’s not the best burger I’ve ever had (that honor still belongs to Hyphy Burger across the bay), but it tastes homemade. It tastes like something I would rhapsodize over if I had a dozen drinks in me. Meanwhile, the fries do their fryly duty, but the real winner is the onion rings. These might be the only good thick onion rings I’ve ever eaten. I normally prefer onion strings, because thick rings are always over-battered and have the texture of infected skin. Sam’s rings are crunchy all the way through, with visible onion in every bite. A miracle. This is very much the same Sam’s that Bourdain showcased all those years ago.

Article continues below this ad

Legends, situated right next door, probably wouldn’t be the man’s speed. Legends, which Emad ElShawa opened just over a year ago, boasts much newer decor, with clean black walls and countertops. But it still exploits the lingering Bourdain brand name to the fullest extent, even if Bourdain himself probably wouldn’t have looked twice at this place. In fact, he almost certainly would have scoffed at its signature dessert, the Dubai chocolate cup. Dubai chocolate is the kind of foodie trend that Bourdain would have resented, started or both. Probably both. But he’s no longer here to object, so I order one. Plus the Bourdain shake.

Article continues below this ad

That shake that bears Bourdain’s name — which includes Biscoff cookies and Biscoff syrup and is topped with Biscoff cookie crumbles — would definitely please his audience. But it’s the Dubai cup that ends up being the best thing I eat at either Shawa establishment. It’s a plastic cup filled with fresh cut strawberries and then topped with Belgian chocolate, pistachio cream and shredded phyllo dough. I had to fight with my digestive system to make room for this thing, but I end up bottoming out the cup in minutes. Dubai chocolate may be a cliche at this point, but this cup isn’t. And if Tony wouldn’t have liked it, that’s not really my concern. I get to do the Sam’s Burger journey my way, which Bourdain himself would have gleefully encouraged. There’s a fine line between inspiration and imitation, and I know which of the two he preferred.

Bourdain died eight years ago and has remained beloved ever since. But enough time has passed now for his immediate memory to begin fading from the public consciousness. In place of the man and his work — his books, his television shows, his restaurant recommendations — there’s a lasting, eat-drink-and-be-merry philosophy that his name now connotes. As such, you and I are living through Anthony Bourdain’s transition from mourned celebrity to something closer to an icon: the kind of historic figure who endures more as an ideal than as anything else. Tony, to use only his first name, is posthumously becoming the Elvis of food and drink. You can see that transition happening for yourself at Sam’s and at Legends. More importantly, you can taste it.

items.title: Why Your Team Sucks 2026: San Francisco 49ers
items.content:
Some people are fans of the San Francisco 49ers. But many, many more people are NOT fans of the San Francisco 49ers. This 2026 Defector NFL team preview is for those in the latter group. Read all the previews so far at Defector.

: San Francisco 49ers.

Article continues below this ad

: 12-5. You wanna get to the part about the owner being too horny for the law, so I’ll blow through this section as fast as is responsible. The 2025 49ers were a shining example of how a football team can prosper in the face of adversity. And by “adversity,” I mean half its roster tearing a ACL, its highest paid receiver contracting whatever mental illness Kanye West has, and prolonged exposure to Mac Jones. I’d award the Niners some sort of medal for their fortitude, but they got rinsed by Seattle in the divisional round so f—k that.

San Francisco’s first loss of 2025 occurred against Jacksonville, after which then-defensive coordinator Robert Saleh and Jags head coach Liam Coen got extra spicy with one another at midfield after the final whistle, in the familiar “these guys are just competitors” kind of way. The Niners also got waxed by Tampa Bay during one of Baker Mayfield’s brief dalliances with MVP-level level quarterbacking, as shown in this highlight. Great coverage on that play.

The LA Rams avenged an early OT loss to the Niners by beating the unholy s—t out of them in Santa Clara. Then Seattle beat them in their house in the final week of the season to clinch the top seed in the NFC. HOWEVER, the Niners still managed to bravely qualify for the playoffs despite all of that, and despite the following injuries:

Article continues below this ad

  • EDGE Nick Bosa: Torn ACL (his racism tendon thankfully remains healthy and intact)
  • LB Fred Warner: Dislocated and broken ankle
  • Rookie DE Mykel Williams: Torn ACL
  • WR Ricky Pearsall: Something about a PCL (he’s already out for all of this coming season)
  • WR Brandon Aiyuk: Nasty case of the insanes
  • RB Christian McCaffrey: Brutally murdered in a standoff with local police (NOTE: This did not happen)

Tight end George Kittle would tear his Achilles in a wild card victory over Philadelphia, thus completing the (leg) sweep. And while it was thrilling to watch the 49ers’ remaining skeleton crew beat Philly on the road, the Niners only won that game because the Eagles are catty meatheads who live for the drama. A trip to Seattle in the divisional round set things in their proper order, and from the opening kickoff.

San Francisco never threatened after that. If they had, they probably would have slipped on a banana peel and impaled themselves on a sprinkler head. The Seahawks would go on to win the Super Bowl a month later, in the Niners’ home stadium.

Got all that? Good, now let’s get to the asshole parade.

Article continues below this ad

: Kyle Shanahan. You know how football coaches will sometimes run wind sprints with players so that they can be like, “You see? I’m willing to suffer just like you guys!” Well, Kyle did those coaches one better this summer when he was like, “I always subject my players to catastrophic injuries, so it’s only fair that I horribly maim myself!” Shanny’s chosen method of hurticide was to wreck the unholy s—t out of his Tesla. This act of solidarity netted the coach a concussion, several broken ribs, a broken nose, a broken hand, a busted eye, and an unfortunate mustache. This is the one time in history when it would have been safer to have Aldon Smith behind the wheel.

How on earth did Kyle crash his car so bad? Well, turns out he’d put the ol’ girl on autopilot mode so he that could check his phone, at which point his Model Firestarter X crossed into the adjacent lane and bashed into another car.

“I’ve had autopilot for nine years, so I’m pretty comfortable with it and, you know, who knows what happened when I turned around? Whether it malfunctioned or whether I knocked it off? That’s something I don’t know yet,” he said.

YOU’RE NOT SUPPOSED TO LET THE CAR DRIVE FOR YOU, YOU F—KING IDIOT. Yes, who knows what happened when you deliberately stopped looking where your car was going? What were you supposed to do, NOT check your phone while driving? What is this, Soviet Russia?

Article continues below this ad

I drove by the crash site in question last week. No lie. I was there in person. The intersection of Alma and Hamilton in Palo Alto is block away from an awkward, very dangerous interchange with University Avenue. It’s a hairy bit of driving even when your eyes are fixed on the road, but this perennial dickhead was like, “Ooh, this is the perfect spot for me to check all the Flock cameras I had mounted outside every player’s house!” And the cops let Kyle walk! And the press sat on the story for nearly two weeks! And yet this man has the gall — the pure, unmitigated GALL — to publicly say “my bad” after news of the crash finally broke? Man f—k you, Kyle. You’re no stand-up guy. You’re a “sit in your Elonmobile and let it plow into a 21-year-old woman who was just trying to make a food run” guy. F—k you and your s—tty car.

Saleh left this coaching staff to go be fired by the Titans in two years. Your new DC is former tragic Falcons decision Raheem Morris. Your new offensive coordinator is one of the Kubiaks. And guess who else joined the staff this offseason?

Maybe that car wreck really did leave Kyle blind.

Article continues below this ad

: Brock Purdy, who is very good but is absolutely not built for this s—t. Purdy has missed time every season, and not merely because he plays for the injury factory. With an aging roster around him — not to mention a corps of pass-catchers who continually step in bear traps on their way to take a piss — Purdy now has to shoulder much more of the Niners’ offensive load than he did back when he was a charming Mr. Irrelevant story. That Brock Purdy was a wee little sweetcheeks who captivated hearts all across the nation right up to the second his elbow snapped like a chopstick in the NFC title game. That’s why the Niners kept reasonable Purdy facsimile Mac Jones as their QB2 for this season instead of entertaining lucrative trade offers for the pending free agent (NOTE: No one was gonna trade anything valuable for Mac f—king Jones).

: [dominatrix voice] Who’s been a bad little boy?

As you can see, law enforcement in Ohio really has its priorities straight. Do I wish that state would focus its law enforcement resources on mass gun violence, hate crimes, corporate malfeasance, and other, much more pressing issues? Yes. Am I glad they chose to humiliate an NFL owner instead? Also yes. The bodycam video of York’s arrest is worth watching if only to see what York was wearing while on his way to get some. World’s ugliest Yankees T-shirt? Jogging shorts? White ankle socks and sneakers? (fans self) WHOA HEY I’M GETTING A LITTLE BIT RANDY HERE. This is what my wife orders me to wear to bed on our special date nights.

Anyway, it’s morbidly amusing that NFL owners can get away with all manner of f—kery while they’re chilling in the white-collar sector, only to have the human trafficking panic come for them the second they make a side visit to Poortown for a little bit of sin. As with Robert Kraft, York has tried to bury as much evidence of his encounter as possible. And, like Kraft, he’ll probably be suspended from the team raw bar for a period of no less than six hours. After that, he’ll be a free, and definitely repentant, man. All rich men love personal growth!

I suppose I should get to the on-the-field stuff regarding this team, so here you go: The Niners’ roster is already pre-deceased. Bosa likely won’t be back for Week 1. Kittle has been activated from the PUP list despite rupturing his Achilles less than eight months ago. Free agent addition WR Mike Evans, who missed most of last season in Tampa Bay with a busted collarbone, is already nursing a bum quad. Mykel Williams is on the PUP list. McCaffrey, already perched on the rim of the age cliff, was held out of camp practices because of “soreness,” maybe because Kyle accidentally ran him over while scrolling Insta at 75 mph. The team’s biggest offseason addition, DT Osa Odighizuwa, had to get his elbow surgically cleaned out in January. Everyone is banged up, and we haven’t even played any real football yet. I think we all know what’s going on here. That’s right: It was the electrical substation, in the Study, with the Lead Pipe. Only viable explanation for why this team can’t stop murdering its own.

Article continues below this ad

The good news is that rookie WR De’Zhaun Stribling is only kinda sorta hurt. Even better, he’s been getting raves in training camp. Now, we all know that if you’re gassing up rookies in camp, it’s only because you’re f—ked if (when, really) they end up playing like rookies. But have you considered that the powerful substation gamma rays bombarding the 49ers’ practice facility could actually be giving players like Stribling Spider-Man powers? Grok tells me it’s not out of the question, and when has an Elon Musk product ever failed me?

More good news: WR Deebo Samuel is back, as is fan favorite LB Dre Greenlaw. Because when Kyle ran back the all-22 from 2025, he said to himself, “This team needs to get even older and more busted.” HEY PRESTO! You’re looking at a potential (2019) juggernaut. Will this team still be able to squeeze 10 wins from a stone? Probably. Will it amount to anything? AHAHAHAHA no. Come on. Don’t be one of those chemtrails people.

Jed York moved back to Ohio because he’s mad about California’s new wealth tax. If you think that living in Ohio is worth that much, you don’t deserve to be in charge of a lemonade stand, much less a professional football team.

Jauan Jennings left in free agency. They still don’t have a viable left guard on the roster. Al Guido looks like Big Dom’s prosperous brother-in-law.

Article continues below this ad

: I’m done acknowledging Kyle as one of the best coaches in the NFL, and the NFL media should be, too. They’re always like, “Oh, [generic new head coach somewhere] is from the Kyle Shanahan tree! Kyle is the best play-caller in the sport! He can take his’n and beat your’n!” Meanwhile, the guy is out there blowing playoff games, bugging every inch of team headquarters, and letting Cyberjesus take the wheel every time he gets a push alert. And for what? Jerry Jones has won a Super Bowl more recently than you guys, that’s how distant the 49ers’ glory years are. And you’re not getting anywhere near them again so long as your owner is looking for love in Youngstown and your head coach has hurt more people than Uday Hussein ever did. Accept your forthcoming mediocrity and f—k off out of my sight.

: San Francisco is still one of the best cities on the planet. I hope it gets itself an NFL team one day.

HEAR IT FROM NINERS FANS!

Article continues below this ad

I was five when the 49ers won their last Super Bowl and have no memory of it.

Our biggest rival is an electrical substation.

Waking today and seeing Jed York’s mugshot is the happiest this team has made me feel in over 10 years.

Kyle Shanahan getting into a horrific car accident because he opted to drive a vehicle that doesn’t need his help to get from point A to point B also perfectly sums up his coaching career.

Article continues below this ad

Their best WR is having a mental breakdown, Bosa probably injected ivermectin to fix his knee, Seattle is going to destroy us again, and Shanny always wears the dumbest hat he can find all season long. We’re f—ked.

Why is everything so weird, man? Why was our coach in a shady, mysterious car accident? Why are 20 players already on the IR, when we haven’t even started playing preseason? Why is half the roster 400 years old? Why is Deebo back (HI DEEBO WE MISSED YOU!)? What is even going on with Brandon Aiyuk and can someone get that dude some help? Did someone hire an Etsy witch? Fess up, Dallas. We know it was you.

The vibes are rancid and the hum and rattle of the transformer station conspiracy theories are seeping into the brainpans of our already-challenged fanbase. It’s gonna be a long f—king season.

We should have drafted competent doctors and physical therapists. 

Article continues below this ad

This team’s window is sealed tighter than a malfunctioning Cybertruck’s. I hate Nick Bosa more than San Franciscans hate the homeless.

In the last 15 years, we have led in the 4th quarter of three Super Bowls, and four additional NFC championship games. All we have to show for it is having to wait longer to hear Drew tell us why we suck every August.

I wish Nick Bosa had been riding that scooter instead of Harrison Bader.

Shanahan still hasn’t learned to coach when it matters or drive a car like a normal human being. I want a Waymo to run me over so that I don’t have to watch this team anymore.

Article continues below this ad

Nick Bosa is a linchpin of our Super Bowl chances and I’m worried this f—king guy might spell linchpin with a y.

There is a zero-percent chance Christian McCaffrey will make it through the season and who knows if Mike Evans will have hamstrings once the substation fields get to them.

I often think about what this team’s accomplishments could be if everyone involved with running it didn’t have their heads so firmly entrenched up their own asses.

I’ve always hated the “Faithful” horses—t. What is it I have faith in, exactly? That by Week 5, all 11 starters will be third and fourth stringers, because the rest of the depth chart met in secret and conspired to all shred their ACLs on the same day? That in the years the team somehow doesn’t collectively fall into a pit full of rusty spikes, Shanny will pull one of his patented 4th-quarter nut-shrivels and piss away a 15-point Super Bowl lead to Patrick Mahomes? That Nick Bosa will show up to every post-game presser in camo and a gaiter, ready to moonlight as an honorary ICE agent?

Article continues below this ad

Now add to that the fact that the world’s largest microwave oven is pointed straight at the practice field, slowly cooking everybody’s insides to the consistency of cat meat, and our coach has such a severe TBI that James Taylor sounds like Metallica, and attempting to hold two ideas in his brain at one time makes his head spin like Regan in “The Exorcist.” And you can’t even feel sorry for the poor bastard, because it’s his own damn fault for driving like a teenager with a Snapchat addiction.

Also, our fans are a f—king embarrassment. No fans are worse than those in Philly, Dallas, and Boston, but somehow we have crawled right down into the sewer with them. The rare times I venture among them online, I find it so humiliating I feel like Cersei on her walk of shame through King’s Landing. Sorry, JimmyBangBang81 from Redwood City, Brock isn’t elite and he never will be. Shouting ALL-CAPS at Steven Ruiz on Twitter will not make it so. Please just shut the f—k up already. 

They share a division with the defending champs and the most feared defensive line in the last 25-30 years. Brock Purdy is about to follow in the tradition of another 49ers legend, Alex Smith, when he has his leg amputated on-field. 

But at least they beat the Eagles.

Article continues below this ad

We’ve reached the stage of the constant injuries to this team where Bill Simmons is bringing up the substation conspiracy and is very close to fully buying into it. Well done, dips—ts. 

There’s nothing more on-brand for a Bay Area team than claiming that electromagnetic signals lead to injuries. When he’s finally tossed out of office, RFK Jr. is gonna get hired as the 49ers health director and cover Brock Purdy in amethyst and animal fat.

Jesus Christ, “The Walking Dead” had more able-bodied humans at this point. 

In less than two weeks my outlook has gone from winning one or two playoff games to, “Gee, I sure hope everyone ends the season with the same number of eyes they started with.”

Article continues below this ad

A team that is old, got ravaged by injuries last year, and somehow had an offense carried by a running back whose career mileage equivalent is the first Model T ever built unironically signed past-his-prime Mike Evans to be WR1 as the salve to their offensive woes. 

This front office has officially run out of ideas just like their grifting Silicon Valley neighbors. 

Brock Purdy will be toe tagged and body bagged because John Lynch drafts like the asshole in a fantasy football league that drafts a kicker in the 7th round and quits paying attention right after the draft is over. Our training staff might as well be a bunch of TB12 rejects. Raheem Morris is our new DC, and at least if he sucks at that he might be able to remind Kyle that we don’t have to keep Christian McCaffrey in blowout games with seven minutes left in the fourth quarter.

Can’t wait to hear the conspiracy theorists explain how the substation is to blame for Kyle Shanahan’s car accident. I hate this team.

Article continues below this ad

When I was checking my luggage for a 7 a.m. flight in Portland last April, an Alaska attendant saw my Niners luggage tag and started talking s—t about how the Seahawks not only won the Super Bowl but did it in my team’s stadium. This, while insulting, still didn’t hurt nearly as much as the other Shanahan-led Greatest Hits, including “Purdy’s Arm Exploded and There’s No More QBs,” “Greenlaw’s Achilles Died at the Super Bowl,” “Tartt Dropped a Game-Sealing Pick,” and “The Fourth Quarter of Super Bowl LIV.” 

I’m reaching the age where “I was alive for all of their Lombardis” is no longer a comeback, but a confession that I’m closer to being a candidate for the shingles vaccine than to Super Bowl XXIX.

It bears repeating that Levi’s Stadium is well beyond the boundaries of San Francisco proper. I am reminded of this during every 49ers telecast when the Skycam hovers over the defunct Six Flags that’s closing soon and parcels of office buildings that are 30%vacant.

Article continues below this ad

This has been a trying year. I had a dangerous mental breakdown in February due to workplace abuse from a co-worker, and it landed me in a hospital for intensive group therapy. In between sessions, the group therapist tried to keep it light by letting us get to know one another. One person mentioned they were a big NFL fan, and so the therapist asked us to go around and name something we loved about our favorite NFL team. It got to me and I couldn’t think of anything. It was 20 seconds of awkward silence and finally the therapist prodded with, “Well tell us who your favorite team is.” It was then I had to say I was a 49ers fan. Without even thinking, my therapist blurted out, “Well, I can see why you are here.” He was apologetic immediately, but honestly I think it was shock therapy, because f—k me here I am thinking this might be the year Kyle Shanahan gets us over the finish line.
